newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Alestra eyes $1 bln local phone plans.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Alestra eyes $1 bln local phone plans.

text.p: Telephone firm Alestra is willing to spend around $1 billion in upcoming radio spectrum auctions to obtain frequency rights that will allow the company to operate local telephone services, Alestra's chairman said on Wednesday.
"The owners of Alestra are looking at investing in technology and in spectrum auctions that will amount to another $1 billion," Jorge Escalona told reporters.

Alestra, a joint venture between AT&T, Grupo Industrial Alfa, Valores Industriales and Grupo Financiero Bancomer, has already announced plans to invest $1 billion in long-distance telephone services in Mexico between 1996 and 2000.
"We are waiting for the auctions of frequencies so we can start working on the local telephone service project," Escalona said.
